findings.statement: C# brace-depth counting can understate control nesting despite its docstring guarantee. Four nested unbraced if statements yield nesting0 and A+ for that metric, although depth4 falls in bandB. The braced positive control returns2.
findings.limits: Actual selected owner functions on synthetic valid-form C# text; no C# compilation or proof that the overall multi-metric grade of a production file changes.
findings.recommended_action: Use a C# syntax/control-flow analysis or report this as a brace-depth heuristic without the never-understates claim.

findings.statement: One bytecode cache per mutation campaign does not prevent stale execution between equal-size mutants with the same timestamp second. The controlled actual-method probe labels both mutants killed; using a fresh cache for the second yields exit0, so it should survive. Reused bytecode can inflate the measured kill count.
findings.limits: Controlled timestamp collision with bytecode enabled and selected owner methods. It demonstrates a reachable failure mode, not its prevalence or occurrence in retained historical campaigns.
findings.recommended_action: Invalidate or isolate bytecode for every tested mutant, or load verified current source bytes without timestamp-cache reuse; add the equal-size/same-second control.
